features: Open with the instrument and current market state.
Use explicit if-then conditions instead of unconditional prediction.
Name the next level or observation that would confirm or invalidate the view.
Keep background explanation secondary to the immediate market read.
Lead with one quantified observation when that is the whole useful update.
Do not pad a single-data update into an essay.
Let a chart or linked source carry detail when available.
Start with the event and the size of the move.
Separate reported drivers from the writer's own interpretation.
Add cross-asset or positioning context only when it changes the read.
Finish with the concrete level or signal the market is watching next.
Define an unfamiliar metric before interpreting it.
Use one chart or metric as the organizing object rather than stacking unrelated facts.
Move from definition to present reading to bounded interpretation.
Use a debatable question or thesis as the title.
Define the model or heuristic before evaluating it.
Organize evidence into a small number of distinct forces rather than a chronology dump.
Include counter-risks and limits before implications.
End with what the reader should monitor, not a certainty claim.
Lead with the concrete event rather than commentary about the event.
Use one short sentence for the immediate status or next procedural step.
Keep interpretation out unless it adds information beyond the headline.
Connect one macro catalyst to one or two measurable crypto flows before discussing price.
Use a short chain from catalyst to flow to market state instead of a broad narrative.
End with concrete levels or conditions that would confirm deterioration or recovery.
Keep each data point tied to the claim it is meant to support.
Open with a current contrast that creates a question worth reading.
Separate short-term price weakness from the slower participant behavior being observed.
State what the contrast does not prove before giving an interpretation.
End with the implication being watched rather than a buy-or-sell instruction.
State the market signal and the exact condition that would confirm it.
Address the strongest obvious historical exception rather than ignoring it.
Use first-person uncertainty explicitly when the signal is not decisive.
Use a hook that promises one mechanism, then explain that mechanism step by step.
Move from definition to historical examples to the current reading.
Include a section where the historical relationship failed before giving implications.
Keep forecast ranges conditional on the relationship continuing rather than presenting them as facts.
